title: An element algebraic over an algebraically closed subfield lies in it
statement: Let $k'$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], $k$ a field and $\alpha:k'\to k$ a field homomorphism (so $k$ is a field extension of $k'$ through $\alpha$ [def-pc-field-extension]). If $x\in k$ is algebraic over $k'$, i.e. $P(x)=0$ for a nonzero polynomial $P$ with coefficients in $\alpha(k')$, then $x\in\alpha(k')$.

source.place: Fields, Definition 09GQ (fields-definition-algebraically-closed, line 901: F is algebraically closed if every algebraic extension E/F is trivial), applied to the algebraic extension alpha(k')(x)/alpha(k'), equivalently the subfield of k of elements algebraic over alpha(k'); its equivalence with the root-of-polynomials definition of def-weil-algebraic-closure is Fields, Lemma 09GR (fields-lemma-algebraically-closed, line 911)
